title.narrative: Provision of Lifesaving Emergency Unconditional Cash Transfers to Improve Immediate Food Access for Vulnerable Households in Bu’ale District

description.narrative: ltpgtThe proposed six-month Food Security and Livelihoods (FSL) project will be implemented in Bu’aale District, targeting 1,575 highly vulnerable households (9,450 people) in underserved, drought-affected rural areas of Buale at risk of displacement. Each household will receive an Unconditional Cash Transfers (UCT) of USD 55 per month for three months, in line with the reduced Food Transfer Value as per the Food Security Cluster’s guidelines due to the funding limitations. The project aligns with the priorities outlined in the 2025 Humanitarian Needs Response Plan and the First Standard Allocation.lt/pgtltpgtltbrgtTarget households will be selected from six rural villages Halgan (550), Horsed (400), Waberi (160), Qodaxley (265), Heegan (120) Baqdaada (80). ltspangtSelection will follow vulnerability based targeting in line with the HCT recommendations, endorsed by the Somalia Food Security Cluster. SEA will work closely with Village Relief Committees (VRCs). Priority will be given to female-headed households, minority groups, older persons, individuals with disabilities, and those with chronic illnesses. It is anticipated that over 10% of the targeted population will be persons with disabilities.lt/spangtlt/pgtltpgtltbrgtIn the first one month, SEA will conduct a baseline Food Consumption Score (FCS) survey, along with joint community sensitization and mobilization activities as per the Allocation Strategy objectives. Registration will be carried out using a VBT approach to ensure proper prioritization, transparency and community ownership. Cash transfers will be disbursed via Hormuud’s EVC platform, the most widely used mobile money service in the area, under a formal service contract.lt/pgtltpgtltbrgtThe UCTs will be provided in three monthly tranches to strengthen household purchasing power, support immediate food access, and enhance resilience to shocks and displacement. A Post-distribution monitoring (PDM) will be conducted two weeks after every disbursement to assess project outcomes and identify areas for improvement.lt/pgtltpgtltbrgtThe project will track changes in food security by comparing baseline and endline FCS results, analyzing shifts in the proportion of households classified as having “poor” (0–21), “borderline” (21.5–35), or “acceptable” (35.5+) food consumption scores. Continuous community engagement will be maintained throughout the project cycle to gather feedback, ensure accountability, and inform adaptive implementation.lt/pgtltpgtltbrgtProtection will be mainstreamed across all stages and mainstreamed activities as per the allocation strategy will be implemented, with women prioritized as primary recipients of assistance. SEA’s strong contextual understanding in Bu’aale will inform effective implementation.lt/pgtltpgtltbrgtIn alignment with the Somalia Humanitarian Fund (SHF) convergence strategy, SEA will coordinate with other SHF-funded partners in Bu’aale to streamline sensitization, registration, and verification activities, promote data sharing, and ensure joint planning for greater efficiency and impact.ltbrgtTo uphold program integrity and prevent aid diversion, SEA will implement robust internal controls, real-time cash disbursement tracking, comprehensive documentation, and targeted staff training. A toll-free feedback hotline 2365 will be maintained throughout the project to allow beneficiaries to submit complaints, suggestions, or compliments, further enhancing accountability and responsivenesslt/pgt
